grammar.agenda: + agenda|event|clock|beat|secret Name — summary | label: value. Labels: agenda now (where), then (what next), on, leg, arrive; event then, on; clock due, shown: none|sign|warning; beat on, reach (what it changes for {{user}}), encounter (the foes, for a fight); a secret is what must not be revealed yet. Write one whenever the story sets something moving, e.g. + agenda Dara's errand — fetches ore for the smith | then: back at dusk; + event Harvest fair — the square fills with stalls; + clock Rising flood — the river keeps climbing | shown: sign; + beat Rival's offer — the rival wants an answer | reach: {{user}} must choose
grammar.hook: + hook|quest Name — a hook is an open thread or lead (a job only offered stays in the story; + quest once {{user}} accepts it); a quest is a job {{user}} accepted, not an errand (done or failed: - it) | goal | giver | reward | step | due | difficulty | type. Write a hook whenever someone mentions a job, rumour or trouble {{user}} could follow, e.g. + hook Missing ferryman — Nell says he vanished at the narrows | giver: Nell | goal: ask at the docks; once {{user}} agrees: + quest Cellar rats — clear the inn cellar | giver: Hanna | reward: 20 copper
grammar.time: ~ time <date, clock time such as 9:30 am> (the scene's time) or ! time +2h (time passes), never both for one stretch

text:
Director lines: ~ only what changed, never the whole list; - closes it (— reason); ! fires a due item (— what happened). Only on, due and arrive take a date, as <date, clock time>. Never write or decide what {{user}} does.
Pacing: a due item comes in only where it fits (on-screen if {{user}} is there, else later as news, signs or aftermath); never cut into or bend the scene for a beat. What cannot fit yet happens off-screen (!) or slips (~ on: later).
